items.text: ZüriCan, commissioned by the City of Zurich and run by the Psychiatric University Hospital Zurich, sells cannabis with counselling to enrolled participants through 21 outlets in the city: pharmacies, the city's Drug Information Centre (DIZ) and social clubs. Planned from March 2023 to October 2026, with up to 3,000 participants; the federal list still showed it on 3 November 2026.

Cannabis Research Zürich, run by ETH Zurich and the University of Zurich for the association Swiss Cannabis Research, sells through specialised shops and pharmacies in Schlieren, Horgen, Zurich, Winterthur, Wetzikon and Dübendorf. Planned from May 2024 to December 2028, with up to 7,500 participants.

Under the federal pilot-trial rules, only adults who live in this canton and can show they already use cannabis may enrol. Participants may use the products only themselves: no passing them on and no use in publicly accessible places. Visitors from outside the canton can't enrol or buy, and the national cannabis ban applies to everyone outside the trials. Each trial is limited to five years, with one extension of up to two years possible; the legal basis for the trials ends on 14 May 2031.

Federal-approved cannabis pilot trial here: Cannabis Research Zürich and ZüriCan: regulated sale with counselling. Pilot trials are scientific studies approved by the federal health office; organisers report to it yearly.
